title: Injective extension of an existing identity-coordinate transpose
statement: Use the internal modules, homogeneous model, free parameter and local evaluations of [def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions] and [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Let UJ be injective and i:N \to M an equivariant monomorphism. If an internal map \alpha:A[G^n]\otimes UN\to UJ satisfies \alpha_S([t]\otimes x)=h_S(x)(1,t), then it extends to \beta:A[G^n]\otimes UM\to UJ. For every f:T\to S, its evaluation on [t]\otimes i_T(f^*x) equals h_S(x)_T(f)(1,t).

proof.text: By the definition of injectivity in [def-sp-injective-resolutions], applied to the monomorphism $P_n\otimes_A Ui$ established in step 1 and the internal morphism $\alpha$ of step 3, there exists $\beta:P_n\otimes_A UM\to UJ$ such that $\beta\circ(P_n\otimes_A Ui)=\alpha$. This uses injectivity of the internal object $UJ$.

source.place: Tag 03EO, lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor (2); Tag 03EV, lemma-j-shriek-flat (2). Agent specialization to condensed modules and identity-coordinate evaluation.

proof.text: Evaluate this equality of internal maps on the canonical pure tensor $[\mathbf t]\otimes x$ at $S$. Functoriality of tensor sends it to $[\mathbf t]\otimes i_S(x)$, giving $\beta_S([\mathbf t]\otimes i_S(x))=\alpha_S([\mathbf t]\otimes x)=h_S(x)(1,\mathbf t)$. Applying the same equality at every $T\to S$ proves the asserted compatibility with all profinite base changes.
